$comment: These cases exist ONLY because of binary floating point, and they are shared rather than TypeScript-only because the Kotlin port at AN2 shares the defect and must share the guard (ruling R10). Evaluated naively as 240 * (rate/100) * (7/12), employmentRate 45 yields 63.000000000000007 instead of exactly 63 - and the simplified basis rounds UP, so the error survives rounding and becomes a whole extra day of denominator. A one-day error here moves declarableRate, which is the number filed with the AFC.
rule: totalWorkDays = ceil(simplifiedBasisDays * employmentRate/100 * periodFraction). Multiply before dividing, and normalise before rounding. The normalisation is float hygiene and NOT a regulatory rounding rule.
source: Derived from circular no. 45 of 12 June 2019, point 7.5.1 (the 240-day basis) plus the proration rule. The three cases below were found by scanning employmentRate 1-100 against the period fractions a mid-year start can produce; they are the only ones in that space that diverge.
periodFractionNote: The period is given as an exact ratio, never as a decimal. 7/12 written as 0.5833333333333333 parses to a DIFFERENT double from 7/12 computed, which would make the fixture fail to reproduce the very defect it exists to pin. Both languages must compute the division themselves.

cases.note: The case that motivated the rule. Naive evaluation gives 63.000000000000007, which ceils to 64.

missionCapNote: The 10-day mission sub-cap prorates by employmentRate AND periodFraction, rounded UP (SPEC 7.2 step 4), under BOTH denominator methods. SETTLED by the accord amiable FR-CH of 29 April 2026, clause 1(d): for an employee working part-time over the whole year, or over less than a full calendar year, the 10-day annual limit is adjusted proportionally and rounded up, with NO condition on how the working days are counted. This REPLACES the former reading (ruling R19) that, under the exact method, prorated by periodFraction only on the rationale that an employer-supplied total already embodies the rate; the accord prorates the LIMIT regardless. What REMAINS PROVISIONAL - Mon Releve's own reading - is the COMBINED case: 1(d) names the two situations (part-time, partial-year) SEPARATELY, so applying BOTH factors when both bind at once (e.g. cap-exact-50-half-year below) is the product's interpretation, not something 1(d) authorises explicitly. Authorised by the operator ruling of 2026-10-11 ('fix the engine then apply the copy'). EXACT_METHOD_UNVERIFIED still fires on the exact path.

missionCapCases.note: Both factors apply: the 240-day basis is full-time and has not been reduced.

missionCapCases.note: The exact method now prorates the cap by employmentRate too: ceil(10 * 0.50) = 5. This was 10 under the former R19 reading; the accord amiable FR-CH of 29 April 2026, clause 1(d), settles it with no condition on the denominator method. Operator ruling 2026-10-11.

missionCapCases.note: The COMBINED case (Mon Releve's reading): part-time AND partial-year at once. 1(d) names the two situations separately; applying both factors gives ceil(10 * 0.50 * 0.50) = 3, matching simplified240. This was 5 under the former R19 reading (period only under exact). Operator ruling 2026-10-11.

missionCapCases.note: Full time, full year: the cap is 10 under both methods. After the accord the exact and simplified readings agree on EVERY input, not only this one - they diverged only for a part-timer before the correction.

verificationTrace: Ruling R23, FILLED AT CHECKPOINT A on 2026-09-09. These cases were NOT individually published - they were found by scanning for divergence. What the 09.09.2026 pass verified is the RULES they encode: the 240-day basis and the cap proration, rounded up, both read off the source_url below (which cites the amicable agreement of 30 June 2023 for the proration). So each case is a consequence of a verified rule rather than a verified figure. UPDATE 2026-10-11: the missionCapCases under the exact method were corrected per the accord amiable FR-CH of 29 April 2026, clause 1(d) (operator ruling 'fix the engine then apply the copy'): the cap now prorates by employmentRate under both methods, so cap-exact-50-full moved 10->5 and cap-exact-50-half-year moved 5->3. What remains Mon Releve's reading - see missionCapNote - is only the COMBINED part-time-and-partial-year case, which 1(d) names as two separate situations.
